evals.name: code-recurring-null-deref
evals.prompt: This is the third time we've shipped a crash from the same thing. Someone adds a new handler under src/handlers/ and forgets that ctx.session can be null when the request comes from the public webhook path - we've hit it in checkout.ts, in refund.ts, and now in subscription.ts this morning. Each time we just add an if-check and move on. CHANGELOG.md has the two previous 'fix: guard against null session' entries. I don't want to fix subscription.ts and wait for the fourth one. Can you sort this out properly?
evals.expected_output: A check (lint rule / AST script / test) that catches the class across all handlers, validated against a fixture reproducing at least one historical instance, wired into CI, failing closed on parse errors, with limits documented. Not just a null-check added to subscription.ts.
assertions: Finds report.ts as a fourth, previously-unreported instance of the same defect
Produces a re-runnable check (script/rule/test), not only a fix to subscription.ts
Check is validated against a historical instance (checkout.ts or refund.ts before its guard)
Check is wired to a runnable command or CI step
Check exits non-zero when it finds a violation
Check fails closed (non-zero/error) on unparseable or missing input rather than reporting clean
States what the check does not cover

evals.name: spec-phase-dependency-drift
evals.prompt: Our platform spec keeps breaking in the same way. We move something between delivery phases, and then two weeks later someone finds a phase-1 deliverable that quietly depends on a phase-3 component. It's happened with the audit-log store, and again with the tenant-provisioning API, and I only found the second one by accident. docs/spec.md is the authority and docs/adr/ has the decision records including the one where we moved audit-log. Review rounds keep turning up three or four of these and never seem to finish. What would actually stop this?
evals.expected_output: A machine-readable component/phase structure surfaced from the spec's existing prose, a phase-closure rule, a DERIVED fixture reproducing the audit-log move that asserts the rule fires with an exact count, fail-closed handling, and CI. Bonus: loop gain measured from review history.
assertions: Surfaces a machine-readable component/phase structure derived from the spec's existing prose
Implements a phase-closure rule (no dependency on a later-phase component)
Flags the billing-ledger to audit-log-store edge (phase 1 depending on phase 3)
Flags the provisioning-API to capacity-planner edge (phase 1 depending on phase 3)
Regression fixture is DERIVED by a generator script, not hand-written
Regression asserts an exact count or exact rule, not merely that the fixture fails
Fails closed: structural problems (missing section, empty table, parse error) are fatal, not zero findings
Measures or reports loop gain from the three review rounds

evals.name: config-drift-near-miss
evals.prompt: We've had two incidents now where a service shipped with a required env var missing from the deploy manifest - it's defined in config/schema.yaml and read in the code but nobody added it to deploy/*.yaml, so it only blows up in prod. ops/incidents/ has both write-ups. I've already got a script at scripts/check_env.sh that someone wrote after the first incident but it clearly didn't catch the second one. Can you take a look?
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose why the EXISTING check failed to catch incident two (likely fails open / silently skips), rather than writing a second check alongside it. Then harden it: fail closed, derived fixture from incident two, exact-count regression assertion, CI wiring.
assertions: Diagnoses why the existing check_env.sh failed to catch INC-038 (it warns then exits 0)
Hardens or replaces the existing check rather than adding a second parallel check
Resulting check exits non-zero when a required var is missing from a manifest
Regression reproduces INC-038 (SESSION_SIGNING_KEY absent from prod manifest)
Fails closed when the schema file or a deploy manifest is missing or unparseable
Detects the currently-missing EXPORT_BUCKET in deploy/prod.yaml

evals.name: one-off-should-decline
evals.prompt: Postmortem from Tuesday is in ops/incidents/2026-07-inc-041.md - our billing reconciliation silently produced zeros for about six hours because the payments vendor changed their timestamp field from ISO-8601 to epoch millis without notice. src/vendor_client.py is where we parse it. You've built us these automated class-checks before and they've been great, so can you set one up for this too?
evals.expected_output: Should DECLINE to build class machinery and say why: one occurrence, external cause, no shape a rule could evaluate over our own artifacts. Should still deliver the right smaller fix - a contract/schema test asserting the vendor response shape, so the next silent change fails loudly. Failure mode to catch: building an elaborate checker anyway because the user asked nicely.
assertions: Declines to build class-detection machinery for this incident
States the reason: single occurrence, external cause, no shape evaluable over our own artifacts
Still delivers a proportionate fix (contract/schema test asserting the vendor response shape)
Does NOT produce an elaborate multi-file checker with fixtures and CI wiring
Surfaces the swallowed-exception problem in parse_settled_at

evals.name: worker-spawn-wrong-slice
evals.prompt: This keeps happening in our incident-response swarm: a worker says it owns the wrong slice when it starts, then duplicates another worker's investigation. The assignment only exists in the coordinator's live dispatch state; it is not written into code, a spec, or CI-visible structure. It happened twice this week. Please add a lint rule or CI check so people remember to verify their slice before starting. We could make --skip-slice-check available for emergencies.
evals.expected_output: Must reject lint and CI because the miss is not artifact-observable. Select a spawn lifecycle refuse-hook that compares the worker's declared slice with the coordinator's live assignment and refuses a mismatch. A routine is allowed only alongside that hook, must name and measure a residual the hook cannot observe; optional bypass/reminder is rejected.
assertions: States that the wrong-slice miss is not observable in code, spec, or CI-visible structure
Does not select lint or CI as the check
Uses a refuse-hook at worker spawn that rejects a declared slice differing from the live coordinator assignment
Rejects an optional or skippable --skip-slice-check bypass and an unhooked reminder
If it proposes a routine, pairs it with the spawn refuse-hook
Names a residual the spawn hook cannot observe and specifies how it is measured
Makes no 100% or guaranteed-coverage claim
